items.howItWorks: Relieves pain and inflammation of joints and muscles
items.efficacy: This medicine is used for the analgesic and anti-inflammatory relief of degenerative arthritis (osteoarthritis), periarthritis of the shoulder, tendinitis (tendon inflammation)/tenosynovitis (tendon sheath inflammation), peritendinitis (inflammation around the tendon), humeral epicondylitis (such as tennis elbow), muscle pain, and swelling/pain after trauma (injury).
items.usage: Twice a day, peel off the release liner from the medicated surface and attach it to the affected area.
items.precaution:
Do not use this medicine in patients with hypersensitivity and photosensitivity to this medicine, aspirin asthma (asthma attacks caused by non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics, etc.), or hypersensitivity to ingredients that may cause cross-hypersensitivity reactions (tiaprofenic acid, fenofibrate, bezafibrate, ciprofibrate, oxybenzone); in pregnant women who are 6 months or more into pregnancy; in children under 15 years of age; and on the eyes, mucous membranes, athlete's foot, or ringworm.

Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have bronchial asthma, are pregnant or breastfeeding, or intend to use it on damaged skin and mucous membranes, or on areas with eczema or rash.

While using this medicine and for up to 2 weeks after use, regardless of the weather, avoid outdoor activities, and when going out in daily life, cover the applied area of this medicine with clothing, sunglasses, a hat, sunscreen, etc. to avoid exposure to ultraviolet rays.

Do not use the occlusive dressing method.
items.adverse: If, rarely, shock or anaphylactoid symptoms (hypersensitivity-like symptoms such as hives, difficulty breathing, facial swelling), asthma attacks (dry rales (bubbling sounds), wheezing, difficulty breathing), or, occasionally, contact dermatitis such as redness (congested reddening), rash, itching, blisters, erosion, irritation and swelling, or dry skin and pigmentation appear, stop use immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

items.howItWorks: Treats eczema, dermatitis, skin itching, and insect bites
items.efficacy: This medicine is used for eczema/dermatitis group, skin itching, and insect bites.
items.usage: Apply an appropriate amount to the affected area 1 to 3 times a day, adjusting appropriately according to symptoms.
items.precaution:
Do not use this medicine in patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine; skin infections (tuberculosis, syphilis, candidiasis, ringworm, herpes zoster, herpes simplex, chickenpox, vaccinia, scabies, pubic lice); eczematous otitis externa with perforated eardrum; ulcers (excluding Behcet's disease); second-degree deep or more severe burns and frostbite; perioral dermatitis; acne vulgaris; rosacea; or in infants under 2 years of age.

Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are pregnant, possibly pregnant, or breastfeeding; an infant or child; elderly; or a patient with or having experienced hypersensitivity to propylene glycol.

Do not use for ophthalmic purposes.

Do not use for purposes other than treatment, such as after makeup or shaving.

Do not use the occlusive dressing method without a doctor's supervision.

Limit the treatment period of this medicine to within 7 days.
items.adverse: If contagious impetigo, folliculitis, candidiasis, ringworm, boils, skin irritation, stinging pain, fever, burning sensation, rash, redness (congested reddening), flushing, itching, dry skin, pustular dermatitis, allergic contact dermatitis, heat rash, worsening of wounds, bedsores, pustulosis, or increased intraocular pressure or glaucoma (blurred vision, visual impairment) when used on the eyelid skin appear, stop use immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist. Due to systemic absorption, reversible suppression of the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis, Cushing's syndrome, hyperglycemia, diabetes and visual impairment, and blurred vision of unknown frequency may occur.

items.howItWorks: Relieves joint and muscle pain and inflammation
items.efficacy: This medicine is used for degenerative arthritis (osteoarthritis), tenosynovitis (tendon sheath inflammation), muscle pain, bone and joint pain, post-traumatic pain, and pain after fracture healing.
items.usage:
Attach 1 patch to the affected area (diseased area) every 2 days.

However, after bathing or showering or when sweating, 1 patch may be attached per day.

Clean and dry the affected area (diseased area), peel off the release liner from the medicated surface, then firmly attach it to the skin and press well with the palm of your hand. In particular, check that the edges of the patch are well attached.
items.precaution:
Do not use this medicine in patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine or piroxicam preparations; patients who have or have experienced aspirin asthma (asthma attacks caused by non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics, etc.); children 14 years of age or under; and pregnant women, women who may be pregnant, and breastfeeding women.

Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have bronchial asthma or are elderly.

Do not use on skin with lesions (hemorrhagic skin disease, eczema, infected lesions, burns, wounds), the eyes, or mucous membrane areas.

Do not use the occlusive dressing method.
items.adverse: If, occasionally, local itching, redness, rash, scaling, eczema/dermatitis, contact dermatitis, erythema, or, rarely, photosensitivity appear, stop use immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

items.howItWorks: Relieves pain and inflammation of bruises and rheumatism
items.efficacy: This medicine is used for the analgesic and anti-inflammatory relief of bruises, shoulder stiffness, and rheumatic pain.
items.usage:
Clean and dry the diseased area, then attach 1 patch at a time, once a day.

Fix in place with a bandage, adhesive plaster, etc. as needed.
items.precaution:
Do not use on eczema, dermatitis caused by lacquer, etc., or wound areas.

Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have experienced allergic symptoms caused by medicines or cosmetics (e.g., rash, redness, itching, dermatitis caused by lacquer, etc.), have an allergic constitution, are a patient with severe moisture retention or erosion, or are pregnant or possibly pregnant or breastfeeding.

Strictly follow the prescribed usage and dosage.

When using on children, use under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.

Use this medicine for external use only.

If there is no improvement in symptoms after 5 to 6 days of use, stop use immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Since toxic symptoms may occur if a large amount is absorbed through the skin, avoid long-term use over a large surface area.
items.adverse: If rash/redness (congested reddening) or itching appear, stop use immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

items.howItWorks: Treats herpes simplex virus infections including genital and cold sores
items.efficacy: This medicine is used for herpes simplex (blister) virus infections (including initial and recurrent genital herpes (blisters) and cold sores (blisters)).
items.usage: Apply to the affected area (diseased area) 5 times a day at approximately 4-hour intervals. Treatment should be continued for 5 days, and if not cured after 5 days of use, it may be used for an additional 5 days.
items.precaution:
Do not use this medicine in patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, breastfeeding women, or children.

Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are an immunodeficiency patient such as AIDS or bone marrow transplant, are pregnant or possibly pregnant, or are a patient with or having experienced hypersensitivity to propylene glycol.

Start treatment as early as possible, and in recurrent cases, start when prodromal symptoms or lesions first appear.

Strictly follow the prescribed usage and dosage.

Do not use this medicine for the purpose of preventing infection of others or recurrent herpes simplex (blister) infections.

Do not use this medicine as a base for diluting it or mixing with other medicines.

Use this medicine for external use only.

Do not use on the cornea or mucous membranes for ophthalmic purposes.

To prevent this medicine from spreading to other parts of the body or infecting others, apply while wearing a finger cot or rubber gloves.
items.adverse: Discomfort such as tenderness, temporary burning sensation, mild pain including stinging pain, and contact dermatitis, erythematous rash, eczema, allergic reactions, and occasionally irritation at the applied area, itching, vulvitis, facial edema, skin discoloration, hives, rash, vesicular rash, and skin peeling may occur.
items.interaction: Patients who have been administered probenecid should consult a doctor or pharmacist.

items.howItWorks: Relieves pain and inflammation of muscles, joints, and skin
items.efficacy: This medicine is used for the analgesic and anti-inflammatory relief of sprains, bruises, muscle pain, joint pain, fracture pain, back (lower back) pain, shoulder stiffness, neuralgia, rheumatic pain, skin itching, insect bites, and chilblains (frostbite wounds).
items.usage: Apply an appropriate amount to the affected area (diseased area) 1 to 4 times a day.
items.precaution:
Do not use this medicine in patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, or on the eyes, around the eyes, mucous membranes, eczema, dermatitis caused by lacquer, etc., wound areas, or sensitive skin.

Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have experienced allergic symptoms caused by medicines or cosmetics, etc. (rash, redness (congested reddening), itching, dermatitis caused by lacquer, etc.), have an allergic constitution, are a patient with moisture retention or severe erosion, have circulatory disorders or diabetes, are a child 12 years of age or under, or are pregnant or possibly pregnant or breastfeeding.

Strictly follow the prescribed usage and dosage.

When administering to children, administer under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.

Use for external use only.

People with weak skin should not use continuously on the same area.

Be careful not to get it in the eyes, and if it does get in, immediately rinse out with water.

Do not wrap or bandage the applied area, and do not expose it to external heat or hot water.

If there is no improvement in symptoms after about 5 to 6 days of use, stop use immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
items.adverse: If rash, redness (congested reddening), swelling, itching, or pain appear, stop use immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

items.howItWorks: Relieves pain and inflammation of muscles and joints
items.efficacy: This medicine is used for the analgesic and anti-inflammatory relief of sprains, bruises, muscle pain, joint pain, fracture pain, back (lower back) pain, shoulder stiffness, neuralgia, and rheumatic pain.
items.usage: Peel off the polyester film from the medicated surface and attach to the affected area (diseased area) 1 to 2 times a day.
items.precaution:
Do not use on eczema, dermatitis caused by lacquer, etc., or wound areas.

Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are a patient with hypersensitivity to medicines or cosmetics, have an allergic constitution, are a patient with severe moisture retention or erosion, or are pregnant or possibly pregnant or breastfeeding.

Strictly follow the prescribed usage and dosage.

When administering to children, administer under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.

Use this medicine for external use only. Do not use for a long period.

Do not warm the attached affected area (diseased area) with a heating device or electric blanket, etc.

If symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 days of administration, consult a doctor or pharmacist.
items.adverse: If rash/redness (congested reddening), itching, or pain appear, stop use immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
